Chronology

A chronology of the life, work, exhibitions, awards, and key milestones of Michele Oka Doner — artist, author, and public sculptor whose practice spans eight decades.

1940s
Origins & Formation
1945
Birth
Born in Miami Beach, Florida
Michele Oka Doner is born to a prominent South Florida family. Her father, Sherwood Oka, serves as Mayor of Miami Beach. The natural environment — coral reefs, mangrove shores, the tidal margins of Biscayne Bay — becomes a foundational and lifelong vocabulary.
Michele, age 13 or 14, 1950s.
1960s
Education & First Works
1965
Publication
Early prints in Generation magazine, University of Michigan
Woodcuts and graphic works published in the University of Michigan's literary magazine — an early public presence for the artist's engagement with mark, symbol, and inscription.
1966
Degree
B.F.A., University of Michigan, Ann Arbor
Completes undergraduate study. Early ceramic and figurative works establish the body as both subject and site of inscription.
Work
Tattooed Torso, 1966  ·  Ceramic  ·  MODCR 1
One of the earliest catalogued works — the body as site of ritual inscription.
1968
Degree & Exhibition
M.F.A., Cranbrook Academy of Art  ·  Hologram Exhibition
Receives M.F.A. from Cranbrook within its legendarily interdisciplinary atmosphere. Presents hologram-based works — among the earliest such exhibitions in the United States.
1969
Exhibition
Objects USA, Smithsonian's Renwick Gallery, Washington D.C.
Included in the landmark touring exhibition of American craft and studio practice at the Renwick Gallery, Smithsonian Institution.
Objects USA Opening, The Smithsonian's Renwick Gallery, Washington D.C., 1969. Wearing early Marimekko.
1970s
Emergence & National Recognition
1971
Exhibition
Gertrude Kasle Gallery, Detroit — Ceramic Sculpture
First major gallery presentation at Detroit's leading contemporary venue. The ceramic seed and vessel forms establish the morphological vocabulary that will persist for five decades.
1975
Work
Burning Branches, 1975  ·  Bronze  ·  MODCR 3
The decisive turn toward bronze as a primary medium. Later acquired by the Detroit Institute of Arts.
1977–78
Exhibition
Detroit Institute of Arts — Works in Progress
Solo presentation including Three Pelvises and Death Masks, presented directly on the floor — an installation gesture that anticipates the ambient scale of later public commissions.
1979
Exhibition
Detroit Institute of Arts & PS1, New York — Image & Object
Landmark two-venue exhibition establishing national presence. Introduces the Pictographs, Soul Catchers, and Altar I to a broad critical audience.
Installation, with Jeremy Doner, Detroit Institute of Arts, North Court, May 1978.
1980s
Critical Recognition & First Public Commissions
1981
Collaboration
Art Et Industrie, New York
Begins collaboration with Art Et Industrie producing furniture and objects at the threshold of fine art and design. The Loam Chair, Thorn Chair, and door handle series emerge from this period.
1986
Public Commission
Celestial Plaza — American Museum of Natural History, New York
Permanent bronze installation set into the floor of the AMNH — constellations and celestial cartography rendered underfoot.
1989
Exhibition & Press
Art Et Industrie, New York — April 5–29, 1989
Solo exhibition accompanied by a full-page advertisement in Artforum — a marker of the gallery's significance in the New York design and art worlds.
Art Et Industrie Ad, Artforum, April–May 1989.
1990s
Monumental Scale & International Presence
1994
Survey Exhibition
Cranbrook Academy of Art Museum — A Lifetime of Accumulation
Major retrospective survey accompanied by a scholarly catalogue surveying three decades of work.
1995
Public Commission
A Walk on the Beach — Miami International Airport
The largest public commission of Oka Doner's career. Over 9,000 individual bronze sea-life forms cast from Florida shoreline specimens, embedded in more than one mile of terrazzo floor. Three years in the making.
Press
Feature coverage, Artforum, Summer 1996
The commission receives sustained critical attention nationally.
1999
Work & Publication
Blueprint of Eden cyanotype series
Cyanotype works in which natural specimens are printed directly onto paper. An artist's publication in limited edition accompanies the series.
Rotunda. A Walk on the Beach, Miami International Airport, 1995–2010.
2000s
Major Surveys & Global Exhibitions
2003
Major Installation
Into the Mysterium — Lowe Art Museum, University of Miami
Immersive environment of cast bronze organisms, natural specimens, light, and darkness. National tour to six venues, 2004–06.
2005
Exhibition & Publication
Hauser & Wirth, New York — Natural Order
Major exhibition accompanied by the monograph Michele Oka Doner: Natural Order (Assouline, 2005) — the definitive publication on the work to that date.
2010
Installation
SoulCatcher Lanterns on native Algarrobo tree, Ibiza
Site-specific installation placing illuminated ceramic Soul Catcher forms within the canopy of a centuries-old Algarrobo tree at dusk.
Installation, SoulCatcher Lanterns on native Algarrobo tree, Ibiza, 2010.
2010s
New Commissions & Major Museum Surveys
2015
Survey Exhibition
How I Caught a Swallow in Mid Air — Pérez Art Museum Miami
Major mid-career survey at the Pérez Art Museum Miami, presenting works spanning five decades alongside new commissions in an immersive installation environment.
2019
Public Commission
Talisman — Park Avenue, New York
A 20-foot bronze column for Park Avenue — integrating botanical forms, cosmological symbols, and the marks of the artist's hand at civic scale.
Exhibition, How I Caught a Swallow in Mid Air, Pérez Art Museum Miami, 2015.
2020s
Recent Work
2021
Exhibition
Marlborough Gallery, New York — Armory Show 2021
Presentation at the Armory Show with Marlborough Gallery featuring recent bronze and silver works.
2022
Public Commission
Palm Goddess for Malta — Republic Street, Valletta
23 × 4.5 ft. cast bronze. Permanent public installation at Republic Street, Valletta, Malta (MICAS). © 2022 Michele Oka Doner.
2024
Exhibition
Marlborough Gallery, New York — Reconsecration
Major exhibition including The Book of Enchantment and new bronze and mixed-media works.
Palm Goddess for Malta, 23 × 4.5 ft., Cast Bronze. Republic Street, Valletta, Malta (MICAS), 2022.

Michele Oka Doner was born in 1945 in Miami Beach, Florida, to a family deeply embedded in the civic and cultural life of South Florida. Her father, Sherwood Oka, served as Mayor of Miami Beach; the natural environment of her childhood — coral reefs, mangrove shores, the tidal margins of Biscayne Bay — became a foundational vocabulary for a lifetime of making.

She received her B.F.A. from the University of Michigan in 1966 and her M.F.A. from Cranbrook Academy of Art in 1968. Through the 1970s Oka Doner worked primarily in Detroit, exhibiting at the Gertrude Kasle Gallery and developing a sustained relationship with the Detroit Institute of Arts. Her landmark 1979 exhibition Image & Object, shown at the DIA and then at PS1 in New York, established her national reputation.

The 1980s brought the first major public commissions — Celestial Plaza for the American Museum of Natural History (1986) — and a sustained engagement with furniture and functional objects through Art Et Industrie. The signature work of the 1990s is A Walk on the Beach (1995), Miami International Airport — over one mile in length, comprising more than 9,000 individual cast bronze forms.

Subsequent decades brought further major commissions, including Talisman for Park Avenue, New York (2019) and Palm Goddess for Malta (2022), sustained gallery relationships with Hauser & Wirth and Marlborough, and continued authorship. She lives and works in New York.
